questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study in an english speaking country. I also heard about the vibrant culture in Melbourne which was important to me. And which was very accurate!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Best decision ever, and worth all the hard admin work!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. The website was very helpful and had a step-by-step guide specifically to exchange students. And a checklist as well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a welcome day where we were introduced to the university and the culture of Melbourne and two former exchange student talked about their experience. They also have "Stop 1" which is a building on campus. They are all very helpful! Just write them a mail or show up! They also have a welcome week, where you can participate in as much as you want. Both about academic stuff and about clubs on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Helpful people at stop 1

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to find a sharehouse (kollektiv) actually through the facebook group called Fairy Floss Real Estate. I found mine really quick, 4 months before my arrival, but I think most people find theirs just before because it's usually last minute that people need roomies.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it is the best way to live with locals. It was easy to get recommendations from them and you quickly got a hold of the social conduct in Melbourne. I loved it!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The real estate in Melbourne has apparently never been this bad - 2024. Not enough houses and too expensive. With all that said, all my friends found satisfaction with their living conditions.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot. But, as long as you check your mail regularly and start the process as early as possible, it can be done without stress. The letters explains everything and wants you to succeed in your application. Sometimes theres a little too much information and guidance though.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was a lot of steps. Get accepted by KU, then by UniMelb, then you need to get a CoE, and visa and OSHC(health). Theres is a lot of steps, but you are guided through it all by uni one by one.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The letters/mails were helpful. Take your time and read them. Ask your supervisor or stop 1 if you're in doubt.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted. You have to decide which subject you want beforehand, but you are allowed to change them a week or two after the semester starts, which is so good! If you have regrets, you can change the subject!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start as soon as possible and take your time with the process. It's not worth it to rush it neither get stressed about it last minute. Stop 1 was helpful whenever the subject registration was annoying.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many interesting subjects, I wanted to study so many more than just the 4!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The subjects I had was on level 1 and 2 which I found was way easier than I thought. You are studying with younger people than yourself, so the teachers are often very helpful with the first year subjects (level 1)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Way more practical which was awesome. Less bound up by books and articles and so on...

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Making music for film and animation
The Business of Music
Big Band 2 (Breadth)
Shakuhachi ensemble

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All!
Making music for film and animation was easy and had a great teacher. For the exam we did a project on a film/animation where we either could compose our own music or use other composers' music. 
The Business of Music had the funniest teacher. Easy subject but also learned a lot. (And Denmark doesn't have a subject like this) 
Big Band 2 (Breadth). Best subject ever, but I had to do an audition beforehand to get accepted into the Conservatory. High standard but doable. The conductor was amazing and the musicians were all so nice and talented!!
Shakuhachi ensemble: Learn how to play the Japanese bamboo flute and learn about Japanese culture. How unique! The instrument was harder to learn than I thought, but I enjoyed the subject so much!!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Travelled more than I thought I would. Buying a bike. Buying and renting instruments.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Less expensive: Eating out, public transport, (free meals from uni), coffee
More expensive: Housing, insurance, visa, veggies

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many clubs. There's something for everyone! I joined the surf club and diving club!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All you can think of. Music, sport clubs and appreciation clubs. Just so many clubs of all sorts, I'm sure you'll find one you love. Also a great way to meet new people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to concerts. Eat out, Melbourne has the best food scene ever!! And omg the coffee, put it in your budget immediately!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
In Victoria: Great Ocean Road, Wilsons Prom, The Grampians, Mornington Peninsula
In Australia: Tasmania to hike, Roadtrip in Western Australia, Noosa/Byron Bay to relax and surf

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very Easy! Everyone's very nice and it has a rather european vibe.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Engage in your subjects. They wanna hear about your life as much as you want to hear about them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
So much slang, but honestly loved it! 
Btw "see you later" doesn't mean later in the day, it can also mean later in the year or next year. 
Cars rule the country.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness of Aussies, the coffee and the multicultural food scene!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1: Priorities whether your study or exploring experience is more important. Level 1/2 if for the explorers and Level 3 is for the study people who spend a lot of time on their subjects. It can differ, but generally speaking, it's like that. Both are good I reckon. 
2: Don't be scared going to the other side of the world. You'll feel more at home than you think. Enjoy the vibe, the culture and the Aussies, they are just lovely. 
3: Melbourne is called "four seasons in one day". Prepare yourself for that. It's not a tropical surf city. 
Oh and the houses are cold! No insulation! Really :o

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it while it lasts, it is over before you know it

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I got in Melbourne means the world to me now. I am so inspired by them and the whole exchange experience which feels so rewarding!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from family and friends I think.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go go go!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
